On his deathbed this man was reminded of the Rugians he betrayed when his murderer proclaimed "this is what you did to my friends!" following which his wife Sunigilda was also killed. The conflict between this man and his successor saw the Battles of Adda River and Isonzo as well as the defection of one side's General Tufa. At Piacenza, this man ordered the killing of Orestes, and one empire was unable to deal with his rise to power due to Basiliscus' fight with Zeno. Julius Nepos made this man head of the foederati in 475, and he met his end at a banquet hosted by Theodoric. Name this man who took power from Romulus Augustulus to become the first barbarian King of Italy.

This man escaped his home country with help from Soviet agent Bhagat Ram Talwar by pretending to be a deaf-mute insurance salesman. The circumstances of this man's death were investigated by the Shah Nawaz Committee and the Mukherjee Commission, which examined whether the monk Gumnami Baba was really this man. Identify this militant leader of the Indian National Army, popularly known as "Netaji," a rival of Gandhi and Nehru who supposedly died in a plane crash in Japanese controlled-Taipei.

The losing commander at this battle claimed that had he "possessed 30,000 artillery rounds" at it, he would be master of the world. The final day of this battle saw half of Jean Reynier's men defect to the enemy and the other half captured when a bridge was blown up too early. This battle began with General Kleist forcing Marshal Poniatowski to retreat from Markkleeburg, and the artillery on Gallows Hill was not enough to defend Liebertwolkwitz. The loser at this battle retreated to France across the river Elster after being trapped between the forces of Karl Schwarzenberg, Count Benningsen, Jean Bernadotte, and Count von Blucher. The largest European battle prior to World War I was, what 1813 defeat for Napoleon soon before his exile to Elba, also called the Battle of the Nations?

This polity defeated an independence attempt in its south-east led by socialists like Eugen Leviné and Kurt Eisner. This government's first leader signed a namesake pact with Wilhelm Groener, in part to deal with a group led by Rosa Luxemburg and Karl Liebknecht. This polity's foreign minister Walter Rathenau was assassinated after signing the Treaty of Rapallo with Russia, and one failed rebellion in it was put down with the help of Gustav von Kahr. This government introduced the Rentenmark to counteract hyperinflation, and its presidents were Friedrich Ebert and Paul von Hindenburg. Name this ill-fated German republic which was replaced in 1933 by the Nazi Third Reich.

Prior to this battle, Tobias Stansbury idiotically left his well- fortified position on Lowndes Hill. The losing commander was a political appointee who had been captured at Stoney Creek after mixing up his own side and the enemy, in stark contrast to his opponent, who had served well under Wellesley during the Peninsular War. Prior to this battle, one's sides forces had retreated to Long Old Fields after the other had come to Upper Marlboro along the Patuxent River. Name this disgraceful American defeat in the War of 1812 which allowed the British to capture Washington D.C.

This politician's "La Baule" speech promoted democracy in his country's former African colonies, and his Defense Minister Charles Hernu resigned in the wake of Operation Satanique. One of this man's prime ministers committed suicide after Roger-Patrice Pelat was implicated in the Pechiney-Triangle scandal, and as President, this man green-lighted the sinking of the Rainbow Warrior. Prime Ministers in his second term included Pierre Bérégovoy and Edouard Balladur, and this man worked with Helmut Kohl to create the Maastricht Treaty. His predecessor was Valéry d'Estaing, and he was succeeded by a man with whom he had a very uneasy cohabitation, Jacques Chirac. Name this longest-serving and first Socialist President of France.

At one battle, this man defeated the Rafael Maroto-led Talaveras regiment, and at another, positive reports from Ramon Freire led him to order an unsuccessful charge, causing his defeat at Las Tres Acequias. While leading his country, this man ordered the assassination of San Martin's former spy Manuel Rodriguez. This man had served under his chief opponent at the earlier Siege of Chillan and Battle of El Roble, which saw one of the reckless displays of bravery that earned this man command over his rival Jose Miguel Carrera. This man led a retreat at the Battle of Rancagua, crying "Those who can ride, ride!" identify this man of Irish descent, the first head of an independent Chile.

Pierre Vidal-Naquet wrote of this action that "One revives the dead in order the better to strike at the living" while attacking a man supported by Serge Thion. Ernst Zundel was charged with this action after publishing some of Richard Harwood's work, but his conviction was overturned by the Canadian Supreme Court in a trial which saw testimony given by David Irving, a leading proponent of this action. The Gayssot Act was used to convict French professor Robert Faurisson of it, in response to which Noam Chomsky argued that, though he opposed this action, it should be allowed as free speech. Identify this act of historical revisionism, which questions the existence of gas chambers and orders from Hitler to perpetrate a certain genocide.

An employee of this man later photographed Indians at Fort Laramie and another employee of him photographed Devil's Slide and Canyon De Chelly for the Fortieth Parallel Survey under Clarence King. The head of his Washington studio photographed an event at Old Capitol Prison as well as a notably moved dead body behind a wall. Another work from his studio shows a blurred horseman in the background and personal effects scattered by the corpse in the foreground, the "Harvest of Death" This employer of Alexander Gardner and Timothy O' Sullivan produced photographs of Lincoln before his Cooper Union speech. Name this most famous Civil War photographer.

Allen Ginsburg wrote that certain people "Lost the wounded look they had ten years ago" after this. This event, in which Dave Van Ronk was barricaded into its location, occured after the closing of the Checkerboard. Residents of Christopher Park were notably participants in it and these events mainly occured on Christopher Street. Activists in the aftermath of this event attacked the Village Voice for refusing to print a certain word and the first Pride Parade happened on the anniversary of this event. Name these riots in Greenwich Village against homophobic policemen that are commonly considered the start of the gay rights movement, which happened in New York in 1969.

One ruler of this government disasterously failed to control a kite. Isaac Titsingh chronicled this goverment, during which Shiba Kokan developed copperplate engraving and Sugita Genpaku published the New Book of Anatomy. The Great Tenmei Fire burned down Kyoto during this government. Matsudaria Sadanobu instituted the Kansei Reforms in this period, during which Kitagawa Utamaro was fined for politically charged prints. Yoshimune's policies encouraged the study of "Rangaku", or Dutch Learning, during this period, although all dutchmen were required to live on Dejima during this period. Name this period of Japanese history widely misunderstood as being marked by isolation.

One religious movement in this state venerated St. Anthony and was lead by Kimpa Vita. The Duke of Bengo's forces escaped a battle along the Ulanga river at which this state was defeated. A breakaway state from here defeated the Portuguese at Kitombo. The Kimpanzu and the Kinlaza were the main factions in this country's civil war and its region of Mombares was a major center of textile production. Garcia II of here allied with the Dutch against the Portuguese and Rui D'Aguiar met with one king of this state. That king sent his son Henrique to become a priest and was Alfonso I. Name this former central African state which allied with Portugal in the 16th century.

This man was the target of an unsuccessful plot by Calpurnius Crassus. The brother-in-law of Otho, this man received triumphal honors after exposing the Pisonian Conspiracy. While this man dismissed Titus Petronius Secundus, he did not execute him until the Praetorian Guard took him hostage. The only public work constructed during this man's reign was a forum later aptly titled "Forum Transitorium." Regarding his reign, Fronto said a dictatorship was preferable to "one who allowed everyone to do everything." He considered adopting Publius Cornelius Nigrinus, but was pressured to adopt a military commander of forces at the German frontier. After his predecessor was killed, the Senate, for the first time, proclaimed a new emperor by making this man ruler. He inaugurated a dynasty that replaced the Flavians. Name this first of the Five Good Emperors.

The death of Mayor Cabell Testerman in this state was rumored to be at the hands of his police chief, who swiftly married the widowed Mrs. Testerman. In another incident in this state, that police chief and friend Ed Chambers were assassinated on the courthouse steps as a retribution killing. That story was told in a 1987 film starring David Strathairn and Chris Cooper and directed by John Sayles. Bill Blizzard was acquitted for treason for his actions in this state, while Don Chafin's private air force of biplanes dropped leaflets and pipe bombs on opponents here. In one incident in this state, Police Chief Sid Hatfield got involved in a shootout with agents trying to evict families. In 1921, this state's Logan County was home to the battle of Blair Mountain, a labor uprising against the state police and Baldwin-Felts detective agents. Name this state, the site of the so-called "battle of Matewan," a battle between coal miners and detectives.

One participant in this event was later shot to death on the ship Kinfauns Castle off the coast of South Africa by a bricklayer. The creator of a document related to this event, Richard Pigott, shot himself in Madrid. It resulted in the brother of one participant, Lord Hartington, leading a breakaway Liberal Unionist Association. Occurring during a walk to the Viceregal Lodge, this event was supposedly the focus of a letter addressed to Fenian Richard Egan in which someone was said to have received "his deserts." It resulted in the death of a man married to Prime Minister Gladstone's niece. A special commission eventually determined that letters printed by The Times were forgeries, and not actually endorsements of this event penned by Charles Stewart Parnell. 10 points, name this 1882 stabbing of Lord Frederick Cavendish and Thomas Henry Burke in a Dublin location, an act carried out by the "Irish National Invincibles."

This battle was where the hilariously named States Rights Gist (yes, that's his actual name) died. Its site featured the controversial construction of a Pizza Hut at the site where General Patrick Cleburne died. Prior to this battle, Nathan Bedford Forrest unsuccessfully argued for a flanking maneuver, but the commanding general was determined to crush John Schofield's Army of the Ohio. James McPherson wrote that this battle proved that a certain army "could assault breastworks." This battle is best known for featuring the so- called "Pickett's Charge of the West," in which fourteen generals became casualties and John Bell Hood's forces conducted numerous ill-advised assaults. Name this November 30, 1864 battle, which in conjunction with the Battle of Nashville, almost completely wiped out the Army of Tennessee.

An investigation of this event cleared Kirk Lippold of blame, while Judge Kimba Wood released frozen assets from a certain country to be awarded to the victims' families. One object in it was eventually taken to Pascagoula, Mississippi, on Christmas Eve after being hauled by the Blue Marlin. Little attempt at reprisal was carried out reportedly because the president was "tired of swatting flies." It was planned and occurred the same year as the Kuala Lumpur Summit held in the hotel room of Yazis Sufaat. After this event, discussion over rules of engagement was prompted by the inability of guards to fire on a craft without obtaining express permission. While a judge declared Sudan liable, the U.S. Has alleged that Abd al-Rahim-al-Nashiri was the mastermind. Name this October 2000 bombing of a U.S. Navy destroyer in Yemen.

At one point in this event, a figure described seeing a painting created by a Scotsman at Arras and also denied having a mandrake. At another point, a speaker dismissed the claims of Catherine de la Rochelle as "folly and nothing more." During this event, Pierre Cauchon, who was later labeled a heretic for his actions, was warned that an ill judgment would put himself "in great peril." At the beginning of this event, one figure refused to take an oath to speak the truth, saying "perhaps you might ask such things that I would not tell." It was reversed after a proceeding authorized by Callixtus III, who acted on the request of one figure's mother, Isabelle Romee. This event took place in Rouen after Charles VII failed to ransom the central figure, and featured a woman vehemently affirming her belief that she had heard a voice from God. Identify this 1431 legal proceeding, reversed in 1456, which resulted in the "Maid of Orleans" being burned at the stake.

This man's family name is attached to a hothouse in Scotland that resembles a pineapple. He hid his family at his hunting lodge Porto Bello, and his soldiers easily won the Battle of Kemp's Landing against the Princess Anne County militia. He fled after a loss at Great Bridge where his Ethiopian Regiment was defeated. This leader lost further popularity when he ordered supplies moved to the HMS Magdalen during the Gunpowder Incident. This man's namesake war ended at the Battle of Point Pleasant and was fought against the Shawnees and Mingos. In 1775, he offered freedom to slaves who abandoned their masters to join the British cause. This man was colonial administrator during Patrick Henry's "give me liberty or give me death" speech. Name this last royal governor of the Colony of Virginia.

A response to this event written under the pseudonym Titus Manlius was the article series "The Stand." An incident following this event led to the Supreme Court case Bas v. Tingy, which created the definition of "imperfect war." An unauthorized response to this event by Quaker activist George Logan led to the passage of the Logan Act. Protestors against this event wore black cockades. William Vans Murray was appointed to resolve tensions following this event, which was done with the Treaty of Mortefontaine. Following this incident, the president gave a speech advocating the creation of a navy for defense. Jean Hottinger and Lucien Hauteval were met with the reply "not a sixpence!" in this incident. Elbridge Gerry, John Marshall, and Charles Cotesworth Pinckney were the American delegates in this affair, in which Talleyrand demanded a bribe. Name this 1797 incident named for three pseudonymous French officials.

Teddy Katz's master's thesis about a community of this people at Tantura was literally put on trial in 2000 during a scandal that saw him defended by Ilan Pappe, a historian known for claiming that they have been specifically targeted for ethnic cleansing. This group's possible decision to falsely claim a mass-rape campaign after Deir Yassin may have triggered an event that was not resolved by the Third Lausanne Conference; that mass exodus of this group is known as "the Catastrophe," or Nakba. Folke Bernadotte was assassinated for his perceived advocacy for this people by the Stern Gang, leading to his replacement by Ralph Bunche. These people were the primary targets of Plan D organized by Haganah, two decades before they came into conflict with a Hashemite monarch during a period known as Black September. Identify this national group that rose up in two major Intifadas against Israeli occupation of their territories on the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

This judge's dissent failed to save railroaded bureaucrat William Remington, who was later beaten to death with a brick by his cellmate. An impromptu speech at a citizenship celebration in central park inspired this man to give an impromptu speech that inspired his popular tract The Spirit of Liberty. The sinking of the barge Anna C was considered by this man in US v. Carroll Towing, which led him to weigh burden, probability, and loss in his conception of a "calculus of negligence."Anecdotes about this man are related in Freedom's Law by Ronald Dworkin, his one-time clerk. This judge held that the nature of a monopoly is irrelevant in his opinion for US v. Alcoa, which he heard after the Supreme Court referred it to the Second Court of Appeals. Name this most frequently quoted lower-court justice in U.S history, a New Yorker whose eyebrows were even more strikingly memorable than his name.

It has nothing to do with Cornwall, but this movement has used a flag depicting a small white cross on black, and it had a quasi-military arm modeled after Mussolini's Blackshirts called Cadets of the Revolution. An attempt to repress this movement was Law 53, or the "gag law," and the Jayuya Uprising was part of this movement. Lolita Lebron led a group supporting this movement which shot Alvin Bentley. Pedro Albizu Campos was a leader of this movement, which was supported by the terrorist group FALN. Police officer Leslie Coffelt was killed by two supporters of this movement, Oscar Collazo and Griselio Torresola, who stormed the Blair House in an attempt to kill Harry Truman. This movement has opposed governance under the Jones-Shafroth Act or the Foraker Act. Name this nationalist movement which seeks to end United States control over a Caribbean island territory.

This dynasty was chronicled in the Hyle Historias, and under this dynasty military service was attached to the preexisting grants of pronoia. One ruler of this dynasty married Bertha of Sulzbach and arranged his son's marriage to Anna of France. Another ruler of this dynasty overcame a conspiracy by his mother and sister to place Nicephorus Bryennius on the throne. A ruler of this dynasty feuded with Vitale II Michiel and subsequently arrested all Venetians in his lands. That ruler led a campaign against Iconium, culminating in disaster at Myriokephalon. Emperors of this dynasty included John II and Manuel I, and its lands were invaded by Robert Guiscard. This dynasty's first ruler feuded with Bohemond of Taranto over control of Antioch, as recounted in a history written by his daughter Anna. That emperor attempted to reclaim Asia Minor by asking for aid from Western Europe, leading to the first crusade. Name this dynasty founded by Alexius I.

This ruler retained Henry Holland to rebuild his private London residence, Carlton House, and he also patronized architect John Nash, whom he commissioned to build the Brighton Pavilion. Despite his outspoken opposition, in the last years of his reign this king assented to the repeal of the Test Act and the passage of the Catholic Emancipation Act. Early in life he had a secret marriage to Maria Fitzherbert, and his only child was a daughter who died giving childbirth, Charlotte, Princess of Wales. He introduced a Bill of Pains and Penalties in an attempt to divorce his wife, Catherine of Brunswick. This man first ruled under the title Prince Regent, during which time Lord Liverpool was Prime Minister, and he was succeeded by his brother William IV. Name this British king from 1820 to 1830, who also held power in the last years of his mentally ill father.

In 1995, this world leader badgered a group of his naval officers, some drunken fishermen, and a tourist ferry to sail to the deserted Hanish islands and invade them for no reason whatsoever; the resulting decision from the Hague awarded him shared custody with his eastern neighbor. This man's former minister, Petros Solomon, has been permanently "misplaced" by his country's penal system following a violent 2001 crackdown on the G-15, which saw him arrest or kill nearly every senior official in his government. Up to 2/3 of his country's populace is eligible for immediate conscription, helping his state displace North Korea for the past five years at the bottom of the Press Freedom Index. This man came to power during horrific napalm-and-trench warfare centered around the Tigray region, leading the EPLF in a civil war against Mengistu and the Derg. Holding power since his country's 1991 secession from Ethiopia, name this President of Eritrea and giant gaping asshole.

A Thomas Nast cartoon shows this man as a genie emerging from a bottle and threatening a figure in a cradle. After the whipping of Allen Huggins, this man apocryphally gave a speech to congress while waving a bloody shirt. Like James Wilson, this man chaired a committee that investigated the Lincoln assassination. This loser of the Bermuda Hundred Campaign was the chief proponent of 1871's Ku Klux Klan Act. Jefferson Davis decreed that this man should be hanged if captured, and he occupied Baltimore as a leader of the Massachusetts militia. While commanding the garrison at Fort Monroe, this man claimed the right of "contraband of war" while refusing to return fugitive slaves. After the war, this man served in congress as a radical republican, and he ran for president in 1884 as the nominee of the Greenback Party. This commander issued the infamous General Order No. 28, which decreed that disrespectful women of a certain city should be treated like prostitutes. Name this Union commander known as "Beast" for his ruthless rule of occupied New Orleans.

In this battle, Lauingen and Zedtwitz prematurely withdrew, leaving one side without cavalry on its left flank. Following this battle the defeated side fell back to the Quadrilateral fortresses. Adolphe Niel was promoted to Marshal on the battlefield here for his actions near Medole, and this battle was fought just south of Lake Garda. Prior to this battle, Franz von Gyulai was relieved of his command, and total disaster here was only averted thanks to a delaying action by Ludwig von Benedek. Hostilities were formally ended after this battle in the Treaty of Zurich, a follow up to the temporary Peace of Villafranca. This defeat for Franz Joseph occurred soon after the Battle of Magenta. A "Memory of" this battle was written by Henri Dunant. Name this combined victory for Napoleon III and the Piedmontese fought in Lombardy, which led to the creation of the International Red Cross.

H.L.A. Hart's Law, Liberty, and Morality grew out of an extensive public debate with Lord Devlin over this crime, the subject of the unintentionally- hilarious Wolfenden report, which euphemized it with the name of a biscuit manufacturer. The author of Ralph Roister Doister, Nicholas Udall, was the first major conviction of Thomas Cromwell's ordinance banning this crime. This crime's infliction upon the Marquess of Queensbury resulted in two infamous trials and the penning of the line, "each man kills the thing he loves" in The Ballad of Reading Gaol. Identify this crime for which Oscar Wilde was sentenced to hard labor, properly known in English legal discourse as "buggery."

Journalist William Bayard Hale sent a confidential report to the US President about this man's regime. Late in life, this man conspired with Franz von Rintelen, leading to his imprisonment at Fort Bliss. This leader's rise was agreed on in the Pact of the Embassy, an action that led to the recall of Henry Lane Wilson. While bringing guns and ammunition to this man, the German merchant ship Ypiranga was seized. This leader ordered the execution of Jose Maria Pino Suarez at the end of the Ten Tragic Days, and his supporters included Bernardo Reyes and Felix Diaz. This leader of the Federal Army had served as general under Porfirio Diaz. Forces loyal to this president arrested US sailors in Tampico, leading to the seizure of Veracruz. Alvaro Obregon led the forces which overthrew this man on behalf of Venustiano Carranza. Name this Mexican dictator who seized power in a 1913 army coup, overthrowing Francisco Madero.

One leader of this organization, Frank Ferrell, was controversially banned from introducing the governor of Virginia at their convention because he was black. Leonora Barry was made leader of the 'Department of Women's Work' within this organization. One major action of this group was crushed by governor Samuel McEnery in Thibodaux, Louisiana. A branch of this organization in Wyoming initiated the murder of at least 28 Chinese miners in the Rock Springs massacre, and its last major activity was led by Martin Irons against the Southwestern Pacific Railroad. This group was supported by the archbishop of Baltimore, James Gibbons, who urged Pope Leo XIII to make a statement supporting their cause. Originally a secret society, the leader of this group was called the grand master workman, and its popularity declined after it was scapegoated for the Haymarket Square riot. Founded by Uriah Stephens and brought to its peak of power by Terence Powderly, for 10 points name this first important U.S. Labor union.
Noble Order of the Knights of Labor

This publication printed several anti-Italian articles written by Arthur Woods about the group known as the Black Hand. Abraham Cahan's novel David Levinsky began as a series of essays in this publication. George Kibbe Turner wrote "The Daughters of the Poor" and "A Study of the Great Immoralities" about urban life in New York and Chicago in this publication, and Crane's "In the Depths of a Coal Mine" also appeared here. This periodical ceased after it was combined with The Smart Set to create The New Smart Set. This publication frequently printed biographies of famous Americans, such as that on Mary Baker Eddy written by Willa Cather, and one on Abraham Lincoln by an author who would later write a more famous series. Ray Stannard Baker's series on US Steel was published in, what muckraking magazine that also printed articles by Lincoln Steffens and Ida Tarbell?

Shin Arahan was a religious adviser to four kings of this state, including Alaungsithu, but his teachings would be rejected by Sithu II. One successor to this kingdom was ruled by the Three Shan Brothers. The Myazedi inscription was carved by the second king of this state, the martial Kyanzittha, who also constructed the Shwezigon pagoda, which is said to contain a tooth of the Buddha. This kingdom began to form when cities such as Beikthano and Sri Ksetra of the Pyu people were invaded from the north by the Nanzhao kingdom, and began in earnest when the Mon capital of Thaton was taken by their first and greatest king, Anawrahta. This kingdom fell when Kublai Khan sent the governor of Yunnan, Nasr al-Din, to collect unpaid tribute. Name this great Theravada Buddhist state of the Irrawaddy Valley, the first to be ruled by the Burmese people.

The United States sent Dwight Morrow to negotiate with this man regarding petroleum interests in his country, and he restructured his country's debt in the Lamont-Montes de Oca treaty. He was originally supported by the massive CROM labor union but later neutered it by declaring strikes illegal. With American assistance this man defeated Pancho Villa at the 2nd Battle of Agua Prieta. His inveterate enemy during his presidency was Anacleto Gonzalez Flores, a leader of the National League for the Defense of Religious Freedom. He only officially held power for four years, but during the terms of Pascual Ortiz Rubio, Abelardo Rodriguez and Emilio Portes Gil, he held the real power – this period was known as the maximato. The founder of the PRI [pree], for 10 points name this Mexican politician who is best known for his anti-Catholic policies that set off the Cristero War.

This man came to prominence when he led an army to assist the usurper Joannes; when Joannes was killed he was awarded the title of count of Gaul in exchange for dismissing his forces. His path to power involved the murder of Flavius Felix, and although he lost to the governor of Africa, Bonifacius, at Ravenna, Bonifacius fortuitously died from his wounds. He moved the Burgundians to Sapaudia after destroying their kingdom at Worms, an event recounted in the Nibelungenlied. This man's greatest accomplishment was convincing Sangiban of the Alans, Gondioc of the Burgundians and Theodoric the Goth to join him in a great coalition to defeat a common foe. Name this Roman general who dominated the reign of Valentinian III and won the battle of the Catalaunian Plains against Attila the Hun.

One king of this region, Ecgfrith, was crushed by Bridei at the Battle of Nechtansmere. Another king, Oswald, was killed at the Battle of Maserfield by Penda but was avenged by his brother Oswy. The first important king of this region was Oswald and Oswy's father, Aethelfrith of Bernicia, whose descendants conquered Deira to create this kingdom. This area was known as the Kingdom of Jorvik after it was conquered by Halfdan Ragnarsson's Great Heathen Army, and St. Wilfrid brought this region under the authority of the Roman church at the Synod of Whitby. This kingdom was the location of important monasteries such as Lindisfarne, Wearmouth and Jarrow, the home of the Venerable Bede. Name this northernmost kingdom of the Anglo- Saxon heptarchy, which lay north of the Humber River.

This text described the Family Compact as a 'petty, corrupt, insolent Tory clique', and its importance has recently been questioned by Ged Martin. This document was once believed to have been authored by a student of Thomas Carlyle, Charles Buller, who did write the related Report on Public Lands and Emigration, and Edward Gibbon Wakefield, the mentor of its actual author, was also credited with its ideas. This document was highly influential on men such as Robert Baldwin and LH LaFontaine, who formed the first 'responsible' government as laid out in this text. This document was commissioned after two unrelated rebellions led by Louis-Joseph Papineau and William Lyon McKenzie. Name this document drafted by a governor-general known as "Radical Jack" that recommended self-government and union for the British colonies of Canada.

The nebulous authority of settlers in this region led to events such as the imprisonment of John Fenwick, and the seizure of Jeremiah Basse's ship Hester by Lord Richard Bellomont. The 'Blues' regiment from this polity rarely saw action and was often ineffective, being heavily defeated at Sabbath Day Point and Fort William Henry. Originally divided into East and West halves by the Keith Line, the eastern half of this region had been sold to Quakers by Lord Berkeley, while the western half was owned by George Carteret. New Sweden had been located in the southwestern corner of this region. This region was home to William Paterson, who proposed a plan at the Constitutional Convention that favored smaller states. Name this colony that was the site of the battles of Princeton and Trenton.

Ademar of Charbanes claims that this man converted back to paganism before his death and ordered the human sacrifice of 100 Christian captives. He may have been killed defending the fortress of Eu from the forces of Arnulf of Flanders. In some sources this man was known as 'Ganger' or 'walker' because he was too large to mount a horse, and he is said to be the son of the earl of More, while the more dubious Dudo of St. Quentin claims that he came from 'Dacia', probably indicating Denmark. This man gained his territory when he signed the Treaty of St.-Clair-sur-Epte with Charles the Simple and he ceded control of it to his son William Longsword four years before his death. For 10 points name this ancestor of William the Conqueror, a Viking warrior who founded the duchy of Normandy.

One man who served in this office was Ausonius, the poet and tutor of Gratian. Another man with this title oversaw the construction of the Theodosian Walls. That man, Anthemius, as well as Rufinus, were powerful holders of this position during the reign of Arcadius. The jurist Ulpian held this post under Alexander Severus, and the crusher of the 2nd Jewish revolt, the wonderfully named Quintus Turbo, was a longtime holder of this position under Hadrian. The transition from Afranius Burrus to Ofronius Tigellinus in this office is usually considered the turning point in the reign of Nero. The first man to usurp the throne from this position was the successor to Caracalla, Macrinus. The originally function of this position was abolished by Constantine, who created multiple posts with this name such as 'of Illyricum' and 'of the East', which was famously held by John the Cappadocian. Name this post most famously held by Sejanus and which was originally intended to be held by the commander of the Imperial bodyguard.

The Manesse Codex was created in this city by one of its wealthy families. Actor Jimmy Stewart was the presiding officer in a court martial arising from the accidental bombing of this city during WWII. The Abbess of Fraumunster was once responsible for appointing the Mayor of this city, and its first independent mayor was the guild leader Rudolf Brun. This city was home to the Affair of the Sausages, where a pastor said the bible doesn't ban the eating of meat during Lent. That man led the Grossmunster Church in this city, and he was succeeded by Henrich Bullinger. Name this city that was home to Ulrich Zwingli.

Either Alexander Buchanan or a man with this first name was responsible for killing the Duke of Clarence at the Battle of Baugé. A king of Denmark and Norway with this name lost the battle of Hemmingstedt while trying to conquer Dithmarschen and had earlier been crowned king of Sweden after defeating Sten Sture the Elder. Another man with this name was a King of Bohemia and a claimant to the Polish throne who, despite going blind in 1336, died while fighting at Crecy. A king of this name abdicated at Stracathro after losing the 1296 battle of Dunbar, which led to the loss of his coat of arms and his nickname of "Toom Tabard". In addition to that Balliol king of Scotland, this name was held by both the first kings of the houses of Aviz and Braganza, as well as by a signer of the Treaty of Le Goulet who was excommunicated by Pope Innocent III. Identify the given name of that youngest son of Henry II, an English king whose loss at Bouvines led to his being forced to sign the Magna Carta.

The losing force in this battle included 1,500 aventuros and one writer said of that side, "Instead of sharpening their weapons, they embroider their clothes." That side also suffered a minor panic leading up to the battle when a sentry shot at Thomas Stukeley. This battle was brought about in part by Abu Abdallah's desire to reclaim his throne, but he drowned in a river as he attempted to retreat. In the aftermath of this battle Antonio, the Prior of Crato, claimed one of the thrones left vacant by it. The leader of the victors, Abd Al-Malik, died during this battle, and was succeeded as leader of the Saadi Dynasty by Ahmad al-Mansur. After the battle the Portuguese throne was filled by Henry, a Catholic cardinal. Name this battle, fought in Northern Morocco in 1578, resulting in the death of Prince Sebastian of Portugal and the eventual end of the Aviz dynasty.

Some of the members of this group were the target of Sullivan's Expedition, and they fought the Beaver Wars with the Dutch and the French. This group's constitution establishes a shell string, or wampum, as an item that can be used to record a pledge. Joseph Brant allied many of its members with Britain during the American Revolution, and they signed the Treaty of Lancaster in 1744, giving up claims to land in Virginia and Maryland. Dekanawida is commonly thought to be the founder of this group, and he was assisted by Hiawatha. Its foundation was driven in part by fear of the neighboring Algonquians. Name this confederation of six Native American tribes in New York.

Instances of this action carried out by forces under Jacques Massu during the 1957 Battle of Algiers resulted in the creation of so-called "Bigeard shrimp". Subjects of this action were allegedly made to "dance for joy" and were told that they needed to be vaccinated for their transfer south, according to Adolfo Sicilingo, who received a 640-year prison sentence after admitting to taking part in this action. Usually preceded by a stay in ESMA, this tactic was implemented most famously under the command of Luis Maria Mendia, whose related ideas about baby-kidnapping led to the formation of the Mothers of the Plaza del Mayo. This action was facilitated by injections of pentonadal and was sometimes aided by attaching cement blocks to its victims. Identify this form of forced disappearance used regularly during the Dirty War, which usually ended with Argentine political dissidents drowning in the Atlantic Ocean after a long fall.

His offensive strategy was detailed in the books The Principle of War and The Conduct of War, a strategy historians such James Marshall-Cornwall blame for large amounts of casualties suffered by his troops. He officially took his highest post at the Beauvais Conference and Maxime Weygand served as his chief of staff. He hosted the negotiations of the first Armistice of Compiegne in his personal train car, which occurred shortly after Along with Douglas Haig he led the Somme Offensive and he replaced Philippe Petain as Commander in Chief. Name this French Marshal that finished World War I as the Supreme Commander of the Allied Forces.

A later incarnation of this event was led by a man comically known as He Man. Two of its leaders were known as Great Healers, and it too place during the Jiazi year. It was in part caused by the abuses of a group including Zhang Rang. That group was known as the Ten Attendants and all were eunuchs. He Jin served as General-in-Chief during this event. This rebellion was led by a man who had the book The Crucial Keys to the Way of Peace and it occurred during the reign of Emperor Ling. That man was Zhang Jiao, while Cao Cao was one of the leaders who suppressed it. Shortly after it ended the Three Kingdoms period began. Name this 184 rebellion by Taoists during the Han Dynasty.

This man recommended stockpiling rubber and tin at the outset of WWII and he served as the head of the Rubber Survey Committee during the war. He gained his fortune working for the A. A. Housman Company and became known as the "Lone Wolf of Wall Street" after he formed his own firm. He drafted a modified version of the Acheson-Lilienthal plan for controlling atomic energy. He was also well known for his habit of discussing politics with people in Central Park and Lafayette Park. He served as the head of the reorganized War Industries Board. Name this South Carolinian financier and political advisor, commonly known as the "Park Bench Orator."

Despite not agreeing to run, one presidential candidate in this election won eleven electoral votes. This was the only time that the Senate picked the Vice President, since Virginian electors did not vote for their party candidate Richard Mentor Johnson because of his relationship with a slave. The Tenneessean Hugh Lawson White denied running for his party in this election. Willie P. Magnum was on one party's ballot for South Carolina, and Daniel Webster was on the same party's ballot in Massachusetts. The keys state in this election was Pennsylvania, which gave its electoral votes to the Democratic candidate and prevented the Whig plan to have the House of Representatives choose from its four candidates. This election saw the incumbent Vice President from New York defeat the victor at the battles of the Thames and Tippecanoe. For 10 points name this election, when William Henry Harrison lost to Martin Van Buren to replace a retired Andrew Jackson.

The only known survivor of this event was a butcher wearing thick ramskins. One person who perished during this event because he tried to save his sister, the Countess of Perche. Priests trying to conduct customary blessings were driven away before this event occurred. The Count of Mortain suffered a bout of diarrhea and avoided this event which took place on the property of a man called Thomas, the son of the master steersman in the Domesday Book. This event led to one ruler proclaiming the widow of Holy Roman Emperor Henry V as his successor. This event traditionally associated with the Quilleboeuf Rock killed William Adelin, leading to a period known as the Nineteen Long Winters, a civil war between Empress Matilda and Stephen de Blois. Name this event that killed the legitimate heir of Henry I and began the Anarchy, a 1120 naval disaster.

This man once said that he had waited thirty or forty years to meet a man who had recently become prominent and called him "sultan of the world." This man's autobiography, the Tarif, contains an interview he had with Tamerlame to try and persuade him not to sack Damascus. This thinker, a longtime judge in Cairo, was a strong proponent of the concept of assabiya, or social solidarity. In his most famous work, he applied this concept to the rise and fall of dynasties or dawla, claiming that each civilization necessarily contains the means to its own downfall due to smaller social units being more cohesive, while development decentralizes state strength. This man's most famous work is the introduction of a universal history which he called Kitab al'Ibar. Name this early historiographer best known for his Muqaddima, a medieval scholar from Tunisia.

The week before this battle saw Brigadier General John Vincent make a hasty retreat west to Burlington Heights, tardily pursued by brigades sent by General Dearborn. Lieutenant Colonel John Harvey commanded 800 men who marched across Barton Township to make a night attack on a force dually commanded by American Brigadier Generals Winder and Chandler at this battle. The American password of the day was given to the cousin of William Henry Harrison, and relayed it through his brother in law, Billy Green, to the hero of the later battle of Beaver Dams, James Fitzgibbon. Sergeant Alexander Fraser led a surprise bayonet charge that took out the American artillery, and captured both American generals who went to investigate the seemingly unruly troops. This battle swung the momentum in the Niagara campaign to the British, who subsequently captured Fort Niagara and Buffalo. Name this battle from the War of 1812, the turning point of the 1813 British defence of Upper Canada against invading Americans that was fought near the namesake body of water.

The historian Eunapius incorrectly said that an eclipse overshadowed the defeated side in this battle that also saw the suicide of Nichomachus Flavianus. Historical texts about this battle relate how the prayers of the victors were answered by a bora or regional storm blowing through the defeated army. It's not the battle of Pydna, but the losing side in this battle famously carried battle-standards emblazoned with the image of Hercules. Diplomatic negotiations before this battle were obstructed by Rufinus, the Eastern Praetorian Prefect. The losers of this battle had erected a monument to Victory in defiance of the victor's earlier Edict of Thessalonika, an action which generated criticism from Ambrose, bishop of Milan. To enforce the dominance of Christianity, a Roman-Visigothic army under Timasius, Alaric, and Stilicho was sent from the East. The Frankish magister militum Arbogast along with pagan-supporting Western Roman Emperor Eugenius was defeated by Theodosius I at this battle. Name this 394 CE battle that reunited the Roman Empire for the last time.

Rendered by the Romans as Diospolis Magna, this city was first settled during the Naqada III period, as evidenced by various artefacts specific to that time, when it belonged to the Upper Egyptian polity of Naqada. By defeating Herakleopolis, this city established the 11th Dynasty, having evolved from being the capital of the nome of Waset, but lost status until the 18th and 19th Dynasties when it lost that status to Akhenaten and Pi-Ramesses. In the bible, this centre of the mortuary industry and precious stone trading is referenced as No'Amon, which comes from New Kingdom Egyptian niwt-imn, which means ‘City of Amun'. The city is famous in modern times for being situated across the river from the opet from which its well-known Greek rendering comes from, and to its proximity to the Valley of the Kings and the Temple of Karnak. Name this ancient city whose other famous temple complex is named after the city's modern name, Luxor.

As Imperial Resident of Seoul, this man acted as an adviser on all Korean government policies, although increasing Japanese influence and the uprising of the Donghak Society led to his recall before the start of the 1st Sino- Japanese War. An ally of Li Hongzhang, he commanded the first New Army, and thus increased his influence at the Qing court, and amid successfully manoeuvering the intrigue surrounding the feud between the Guangxu Emperor and Empress Dowager Cixi, he developed China's first professional police force in Tianjin, and established the powerful Beiyang Army, which gave him the balance of power between the Qing court and revolutionaries. With help from his ally Duan Qirui, he managed to be elected Provisional President in opposition to the Kuomintang, and used his victory over its proclaimed ‘Second Revolution' to centralize power in himself. Name this Chinese statesman who attempted to establish himself as the head of his Great Chinese Empire.

This period began with a botched kidnapping that resulted in the death of banker Jurgen Ponto. An airplane pilot was executed in Aden for trying to contact authorities during this period after being forced to fly to Rome, Cyprus, Bahrain, and Dubai. An early part of this period involved using a baby carriage to stop the motorcade of the industrialist Hanns-Martin Schleyer to kidnap him. A later part of this period was ended by Operation Fire Magic in Mogadishu where GSG-9 killed all but one member of a Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine cell that had hijacked the Landshut. The motivation for the terrorist actions of this period was to release prisoners in Stammheim Prison who had started the Baader-Meinhoff Group. Name this period of terrorism perpetrated by the Red Army Faction.

This man defeated Maximilian III of Austria at Pitschen to a throne that that he had no right to. This man's royal forces won the Battle of Guzow against the rebellion of Zebrzydowski after he attempted to limit the rights of his nobility. This man intervened in the affairs of his Eastern neighbour after Vasilii Shuisky allied with his uncle who had taken Estonia from him. This man's son was chosen by the Seven Boyars as a suitable leader if Orthodoxy was maintained. Instead, Minin and Pozharsky defeated this ruler after he tried to take the Russian throne himself, which forced him to sign the Treaty of Deulino, which gave his nation Smolensk. This son of John III of Sweden was deposed by Charles IX from that throne for being a Catholic, ending the personal union under his reign with the Commonwealth where he succeeded Stephen Bathory. Name this Polish king during the Time of Troubles.

The Fifth Institutional Act of this country established a military dictatorship after a coup deposed a leader who reimposed presidential supremacy and was opposed by the Marches of the Family with God for Freedom. General Ernesto Geizel was president of this country under the ARENA party, ended its torture of leftists, and began transitioning to democracy. Another leader of this country campaigned on the motto "fifty years of progress in five." This nation's finance minister for the successor of the impeached Fernando Collor introduced the Plano Real social initiative. That was expanded into the Bolsa familia by the successor of Fernando Cardoso as president of this country. Name this country whose presidents have included Juscelino Kubitschek and Lula da Silva.

The goal of this venture was later realized by an expedition under Forbes. Some historians pin the blame on the namesake commander of this expedition, who utilized European-style fighting styles in the American wilderness. The namesake commander of this venture died of wounds during the retreat, and was buried near the site of an earlier battle where a colonial commander was defeated after causing an affair at the Jumonville Glen. This venture was ambushed by a smaller French, Canadian, and Native American force, and thus failed to capture Fort Dusquesne. Sent out after the defeat of George Washington at Fort Necessity, this expedition which ended in defeat at Monogahela was the first major engagement of the North American Theatre of the Seven Years' War. Name this joint British and American 1755 colonial expedition into the Ohio Valley.

The third battalion of one of this country's regiments joined Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry in holding off Chinese attacks at Kapyong during the Korean War. This country's troops successfully held Fire Support Base Coral in another war. One ship from this country's navy was lost after a battle with the German auxiliary cruiser Komoran. This country successfully fought for control of the Kokoda Track on New Guinea against the Japanese during the Second World War. In the First World War, this country's light horse made a bayonet charge on Turkish positions at Beersheeba during the Third Battle of Gaza. Under the command of John Monash, its namesake Corps, along with the Canadian Corps, spearheaded the Hundred Days' Offensive. However, this country may be best known providing the bulk of a corps that often swam in its namesake cove during an attempt to seize the Dardanelles. Name this Commonwealth country whose troops contributed non-New Zealander troops to the ANZACs.

One member of this house was the pope who issued a bull against enslavement of the inhabitants of the New World, Sublimus Dei and who authorized the creation of the Jesuits in the spirit of the Council of Trent that he convened; that member of this family was Paul III. A botanical garden on the Palatine Hill is named for this noble house. Alessandro of this house commissioned that garden and was the son of the Pier Luigi also of this house who received the duchies of Piacenza and Castro. Another member of this house, Elizabeth, was the wife of King Philip V of Spain and influenced her husband to launch what became the War of the Quadruple alliance so her second son could become the duke of this family's ancestral Italian holdings. Name this Italian noble house, longtime rulers of the Duchy of Parma.

The Julius Pratt Company gave an ivory cane to the leading opponent of this proviso, leaving blank space on the inscription for the anticipated date of its repeal. In the Senate, it was enacted through a technical maneuver involving votes on whether to vote. One bill which provided for this regulation was introduced by George Patton's great-grandfather, and another is named for New Hampshire's Charles Atherton. A maneuver againt it involved the "nine ladies from Fredricksburg" and the strategic omission of the intent of a piece of paper which Julius Caesar Alford made a motion to set on fire. Joshua Giddings played a key role in repealing this proviso in 1844, along with the man who constantly tested its limitations, Massachussetts Representative John Quincy Adams. Name this standing rule of the House of Representatives, adopted in 1836 at the behest of Southern Congressmen, which prohibited the consideration of any petition regarding slavery.

This man had half of his left index finger amputated when Willis Dickerson bit it off following this man's kicking of Dickerson in the groin. This man's brother made a fortune running whiskey into dry Oklahoma and importing opium across the Mexican border, which gained this man contacts with Paul Jones during Tony Accardo's attempt to corrupt county sheriff Steve Guthrie. He was involved in a lawsuit with a stripper named "Jada" after he brusquely turned off the spotlight at the Carousel Club. Two notable committee reports differ over whether this man spoke to Seth Kantor at Parkland Hospital. While impersonating a reporter, this man corrected Henry Wade at a press conference after Wade confused the Crusade to Free Cuba Committee with the Fair Play for Cuba Committee. His attorney, Melvin Belli, stated that this man's original story was that he was trying to spare "Caroline" and a recent widow from having to testify at a trial. Name this peripheral organized crime figure who walked into Dallas police headquarters with a gun on November 24, 1963 and murdered Lee Harvey Oswald.

The larger part of this institution survived during the period of the Old Covenant, though one of its offices was replaced with a new dual position called "logmenn." One leader of this body insisted that the eating of horse meat and the practice of infanticide be allowed to continue, but otherwise ordered the Christianization of the country governed by this body. The location of this body's meetings was chosen after the master of Bláskógar had his land confiscated following a murder conviction. This institution's meetings, which were dominated by "gothat," each began with a recitation from the Law Rock. A forty-three year interruption in this body's meetings followed its dissolution by Christian VII of Denmark in 1800; it had previously lost much of its power to the King of Norway. Identify this legislature which first met in the tenth century, whose name is still used for the parliament of Iceland.

One person with this social status acted as a double agent during the Battle of Salamis, pretending to defect to Xerxes in order to lure the Persian ships into the trap. This status was held by Sinnicus, and the kheirotekhnai were a subgroup of artisans within this class. The Decelea garrison worked on Sparta's behalf in the Peloponnesian War by encouraging twenty thousand of these people to leave Athens. Some people were relieved of this status by the Seisachtheia, after which only unmarried non-virgins could be put into this status for monetary reasons. Solon's legal reforms also included a prohibition on these people joining wrestling academies or attempting to engage in pedophilic relationships. These people occupied a social position below that of the resident aliens or "metics" and had a defined right against being arbitrarily killed. Identify this lowest class of most Greek city-states, consisting of debtors, war captives, and other unfree persons.

One of these people was a literary critic who wrote The Enemy That Never Was and killed himself after being accused of plagiarism a second time. Ian Mackenzie proclaimed that there should be none of these people "from the Rockies to the seas." Some of these people were forced to work on sugar beet plantations. Others built the Yellowhead Highway, and others were moved to locations such as Kaslo, New Denver, and Sandon. Clashes between these people and other ethnic groups over fishing jobs were a constant feature of one province's politics in the early twentieth century, leading to widespread popular support for the liquidation of their property which occurred during World War II. Name this immigrant population which Brian Mulroney offered compensation to for their wartime internment.

The namesake capital of this kingdom was home to the tallest obelisk in human history, which has since fallen over, among 126 total obelisks here. One monarch of this kingdom, who donated his crown to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre after abdicating, became known at Saint Elesbaan for his war against Dhu Nawas. This kingdom is the setting of a work about the transfer of th Ark of the Covenant to this place by the son of Makeda, the Kebra Negast. After a visit from Frumentius, its King Ezana became the first ruler in the world to convert to Christianity. Identify this first millenium CE kingdom which warred with the Jewish Himyarites and was the origin of contemporary Ethiopia.

One diehard opponent of this cause was the former "Terror of the Bandits" in Java who refused to surrender his ship to this cause's proponents, instead screaming "I'd rather be blown up than--" while throwing his lit cigar into a barrel of gunpowder and blowing up his ship with all aboard. An army fighting for this cause was defeated at Leuven and Hasselt, and this cause's success led to the birth of an irredentist movement called Orangism. This cause was fought for during the Ten Days Campaign, which was sparked by hearing the aria "Sacred Love of Fatherland" during a performance of The Mute Girl of Portici. A longer-term resentment leading to this cause was the periodic attempt to impose Dutch as an official language on the Walloons. Identify this cause which was secured in 1830 by the accession of Leopold I to the throne of a new Low Country.

As a princess, Lili'uokalani returned from attending this event to find that the Bayonet Constitution had stripped much of her father's power. A poem written on the occasion of this event notes that "the Nile spills his overflow beside the Severn's dead," and begins "From Clee to heaven the beacon burns, the shires have seen it plain." That poem was titled for the year of this event and written by A.E. Housman. James Monro was made Police Commissioner largely for his work foiling a Fenian plot to dynamite Westminster Abbey during this event. Fifty foreign kings and princes were invited to this event, which served as a return to public life for its subject, who had largely entered seclusion after the death of Prince Albert. Name this 1887 spectacle, the fiftieth anniversary of the coronation of a British monarch.

Newsman James Davidson accused one military leader during this conflict of planning to steal treasure from a city, which caused the city's residents to drag the commander out of his chair by his hair and beat the shit out of him. During this conflict, the cruiser Volta threatened to attack one city if they did not give it coal. Robert Hart helped draft the agreement that ended this war. The city of Keelung was target of naval bombardment in one of this war's campaigns. During a river battle near the start of this war, one side's flagship, the Yangwu, was destroyed by spar torpedo. This war was preceded by one side's war with the Black Flag Army. It's not an Opium War, but this war was concluded with the Treaty of Tianjin. A few months before this war began in earnest, the two sides clashed at Bac Le. This war ended with one side taking control of Tonkin. Name this clash between the historical and colonial foreign rulers of Vietnam.

During this battle, Ulysses S. Grant sent a telegram to Washington claiming "I propose to fight it out on this line, if it takes all summer." While the frontal attack on Laurel Hill failed, Emory Upton found some success in this battle by innovatively ordering his men to charge the Confederate positions without pausing to fire and reload. It was the site of the highest ranking Union casualty in the war, when John Sedgwick was killed by a sniper. While this battle raged, Grant dispatched Philip Sheridan at the head of a massive cavalry unit which won the Battle of Yellow Tavern, mortally wounding J.E.B. Stuart. The bloodiest battle of the Overland Campgain, this battle included intense fighting at a portion of the Mule Shoe known as the Bloody Angle. Name this 1864 Civil War battle which took place near a Virginia courthouse just after the Battle of the Wilderness.

The Roman gladiator class called the dimachaeri fought with one of these weapons in each hand. In Scotland, a large variant of this weapon called a "claymore" was used. A German weapon of this type was called the Katzbalger because it was carried in cat's skin. Jordanes claimed that Attila had been given one of these weapons by a shepherd whose flocks had discovered it in a field. The German mercenaries known as Landsknecht were usually armed with one of these weapons called a "zweihander." In ancient Rome, cavalrymen wielded a weapon of this type called the "spatha," while foot soldiers carried one called the "gladius." name this type of weapon which can be called a scimitar when it is curved.

Soldiers in this military force who misbehaved were punished by being shackled to the "clog." This military force was aided by the Skinners who raided for supplies and hunted the so called Cowboys. Recruitment quotas for this organization were increased as a part of the 88-Battalion Resolve. In an effort to defend one region, this military established the Flying Camp. This organization's field manual, Regulations for the Order And Discipline of the Army, was more commonly known as the Blue Book. Scottish doctor James Craik worked for this military. This military took over one city shortly after an opposing force left on Evacuation Day. Veterans of this military force established the Society of the Cincinnati. The main infantry component of this was organized into the "State Lines" and Friedrich Steuben drilled this fighting force at Valley Forge. Name this main army lead by George Washington that fought the British.

This man's father was executed after putting down Firmus's rebellion against Romanus. Early in this man's rule, his general, Modares, had a number of victories in the Balkans. This leader had Demophilus expelled from Constantinople. Along with his much younger colleague, he fought a civil war against the usurper Magnus Maximus and later this man won the battle of the Frigidus against the usurping Arbogast and Eugenius. This man was made emperor by his temporary colleague, Gratian. He was succeeded by his children Arcadius and Honorius. St. Ambrose excommunicated this emperor over a massacre in Thessalonica and this man had earlier called the First Council of Constantinople. He effectively outlawed paganism in the empire. Name this last Emperor to rule both the Eastern and Western Roman Empires, who died in 395 CE.

This ruler's wife had a maid nicknamed The Partridge who was much disliked by the populace for her attempts to meddle in affairs of state. This ruler's brother demanded that at a minimum "the king's hair should be combed" in one attempt to gain power. During this man's reign, the Duke of Medinaceli established the Board of Trade and Currency to crack down on guilds. While this ruler was still young, this country was effectively controlled by Eberhard Nithard. The Collection of Laws of the Indies was compiled on this ruler's authority. This ruler's second marriage was to Maria Anna of Neubur. Frolian Diaz arranged for this ruler to be exorcised on the theory that he had been bewitched through a cup of chocolate. He regained Catalonia through the Treaty of Ryswick. This king's extreme developmental problems have been attributed to his bad Hapsburg genes. Name this king whose death lead to the War of the Spanish Succession.

After being called Judas by a constituent, this man replied "‘Judas was paid! Judas was paid! I am making a sacrifice!" With Angus Maude, this man wrote the pamphlet Change is our Ally which called for economic liberalization and he wrote a work about parliamentary history, Great Parliamentary Occasions. As Financial Secretary to the Treasury, this man convinced the Chancellor of the Exchequer, Peter Thorneycroft, to raise interest rates. This fluent Urdu speaker entered parliament because he wanted to be Viceroy of India. He ordered the destruction of the lunatic asylums while Minister of Health. This man gave decried the "great administrative disaster" of the Hola Massacre and in a speech on the topic declared "We must be consistent with ourselves everywhere." He put forth the "Morecambe budget" in an attempt to lower government spending. At the Midland Hotel, this man talked about a woman who had shit put through her letterbox because she refused to rent out rooms. This man decided to stay in Parliament because he thought Idi Amin's expulsion of Asians would trigger a new wave of immigration. Name this British politician who gave the "Rivers of Blood" speech about immigration.

Admiral Bancroft Gherardi was sent to this country in 1891 in an effort to coerce it into giving favorable terms to the Clyde Steamship Line and leasing a harbor to the U.S Military. In 1857, Peter Duncan claimed an island off this country's western coast for the United States and that island was the site of an 1889 revolt and race riot by guano miners from Maryland. Admiral William B. Caperton deployed troops from USS Washington here during one military action and FDR wrote one of this country's constitutions. Smedley Butler fought the Cacos here while serving as head of its police force. Benjamin Harrison appointed and then fired Frederick Douglas to the position of minister to this country. This country and the U.S. Still dispute who controls Navassa Island. Between 1915 and 1934, this country was occupied by the United States. In 1994, the U.S. Used the threat of force in Operation Uphold Democracy to return the overthrown president of this country to power. Name this country that used to be lead by Jean Bertrand Aristide.

Some students flew black dove-shaped kites to protest the opening ceremony of these Olympic Games. This was the first Olympics in which East Germany and West Germany competed separately. Dick Fosbury's gold medal at these Games made the Fosbury Flop the mainstream high jump technique. Czech gymnast Vera Caslavska quietly looked away during the playing of the Soviet anthem, resulting in her forced retirement. Ten days before these Olympics, student protesters at the Three Cultures Square at Tlatelolco Plaza were violently massacred. Perhaps the most controversial aspect of these games occurred during the medal ceremony for the 200m, when John Carlos and Tommie Smith gave a Black Power salute. Name this Summer Olympics held in Mexico City.

The ninth holder of this office was forced to flee to Mongolia in 1924 after refusing to pay a hefty tax needed to support military efforts. Holders of this position usually sit at the Tashilhunpo Monastery, a tradition which began when Khedrup Je, the abbot of the monastery, was appointed as the first of them. The name of this position translates to "Great Scholar." Each of them is thought to be an incarnation of the Amitabha Buddha. An ongoing controversy over who holds this position began in 1995, when Gedhun Choekyi Nyima went missing and Chinese authorities used the Golden Urn to select Gyaincain Norbu instead. This position's most politically important role is in selecting the next Dalai Lama. Name this second most revered position in Tibetan Buddhism.

One leader with this name only ruled for three months before abdicating in favor of Marwan I. That leader reluctantly succeeded his father Yazid I and inherited the struggle against Abdullah bin Zubayr. Another man with this name was crowned as Caliph in Jerusalem and introduced the "barid" postal service. That man captured Rhodes and sold the remains of the Colossus to a merchant with 900 camels. That leader with this name was appointed governor of Syria by Caliph Umar. That ruler fought the indecisive Battle of Siffin and waged a protracted war against Ali on the pretense of avenging the death of his kinsman Caliph Uthman. Give this name shared by the first and third leaders of the Umayyad Caliphate.

After the main branch of this party converted a key regional ruler in the so-called Northeast Flag Replacement, several offshoots of this party challenged it in the Central Plains War. Rebellions against this party's rule included the Kumul Rebellion and the Charkhlik Revolt. The Blue Shirts affiliated with this party helped it to launch the New Life Movement, which synthesized traditional religious principles with modern nationalism and which was based on the Three Principles of the People articulated by this party's founder. This party's military wing was trained at the Whampoa Military Academy to participate in the Northern Expedition. After this party's leader was kidnapped in the Xi'an Incident, it had to form a United Front with its Marxist opponents based in Yan'an. Name this nationalist party led by Chiang Kai-shek when it was defeated by the Chinese Communists.

The first time Henry II received communion after ordering the murder of Thomas Beckett occurred in this cathedral, which had originally been built after Sitric Silkbeard returned from a pilgrimage to Rome. Richard de Clare, Earl of Pembroke, who was nicknamed Strongbow, was originally buried in this cathedral after overseeing its expansion. Lambert Simnel was crowned king in this cathedral, whose original main stone section was designed by St Laurence O'Toole. During the Reformation, Edward VI gave all of the jewels and ornaments from St Patrick's Cathedral to this cathedral, but Mary I soon gave them all back. The main Anglican cathedral in Dublin is, what cathedral that shares its name with an Oxford college founded by Cardinal Wolsey and the most populous city on New Zealand's South Island?

As World War II ended, this country's troops were required to stay east of the Morgan Line. A wartime agreement among anti-Nazi groups in this country was the short-lived Treaty of Vis.
